newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi says not too worried about growing trade gap.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi says not too worried about growing trade gap.

text.p: Vietnam is not overly worried about its ballooning trade deficit because most of its imports are capital goods to be used for future production and potential exports, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
"Though the trade imbalance exists, the issue shouldn't cause too much concern because the import structure is mainly development investment," he told a briefing for reporters.
The official Vietnam News Agency said on Monday that the country posted a record trade deficit of $3.25 billion in the first eight months of this year.
Imports rose 45 percent from the same 1995 period to $7.60 billion while exports rose 22.6 percent to $4.35 billion.
The spokesman said the "import surplus" was, to a considerable extent, due to newly arrived foreign companies investing in construction or preparing for production.
"This is a common phenomenon seen in various countries in their initial stage of industrialisation and modernisation," he said.
He added that the government had set a policy for effective investment to boost exports, which would cut the trade deficit and help repay debts.

The General Statistics Office said last month that it was necessary to review foreign investment licensing to achieve a balance between infrastructure projects and industries with long production cycles and others where output was more rapid.
